topic: Dataverse Plugin for Coding Agents Guide 2026: Build Enterprise Apps From Agent Prompts

key_points: Primary Microsoft Build 2026 story uses three personas: developer building a data model, RevOps analyst querying CRM, and platform admin configuring security.

Strongest examples are concrete enterprise workflows: spreadsheet-to-Dataverse import, natural-language pipeline prep, field-level security, business units, access teams, auditing, and impersonation-style validation.
Content gap: inspirational launch narrative, but not a hands-on guide for prerequisites, setup, prompt design, governance, or troubleshooting.
Announces Dataverse Skills as an open-source plugin for GitHub Copilot and Claude Code.
Explains the connect-build-operate model: environment discovery/authentication, solution/table/form/view creation, data loading, querying, and data profiling.
Useful positioning: the user prompts in natural language while the agent chooses skills, PAC CLI, MCP, Python SDK, or Web API as needed.
Independent competitor article frames the plugin as a governance shift, not just a productivity feature.
Highlights the tension between fast natural-language operations and enterprise controls for data quality, write-backs, security, and auditability.
Useful angle to beat: turn the governance checklist into practical sections with recommended environment policies, approval points, and validation evidence.
Practical how-to competitor covering Claude Code/GitHub Copilot installation, MCP client enablement, endpoints, and first prompt.
Includes common setup errors such as MCP client not allowed, missing PAC CLI, no active auth profile, and schema/logical-name issues.
Useful gap: article is setup-heavy; a stronger guide can add production readiness, prompt patterns, security boundaries, cost caveats, and comparison of agent clients.
Official open-source repository describes the plugin as supporting Claude Code and GitHub Copilot for building, querying, and managing Dataverse through natural language.
Repository activity shows expanding client support, including Cursor and Codex-related plugin work by June 2026.
The repo is a useful source for current installation details, skill catalog, versions, and contribution/evaluation signals.
Official Microsoft Learn docs define Dataverse as an MCP server for Copilot Studio, VS Code GitHub Copilot, GitHub Copilot CLI, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and other MCP clients.
Lists GA MCP tools such as search_data, search, create_record, update_record, delete_record, create_table, update_table, delete_table, read_query, describe, and skill/file tools.
Important monetization point: external AI-agent access to Dataverse MCP tools has Copilot Credit billing rules starting December 15, 2025.

stats.fact: Microsoft's Build 2026 Dataverse plugin post was published June 4, 2026 and says the plugin is available on the Claude and GitHub Copilot marketplaces.
The Dataverse Skills developer announcement says the plugin is open source, MIT-licensed, and composed of standalone Markdown skills with YAML frontmatter.
Microsoft Learn lists the Dataverse MCP server URL pattern as https://{dataverseOrgName}.crm.dynamics.com/api/mcp.

Microsoft Learn says Dataverse MCP currently exposes tools for data search, metadata search, record create/update/delete, table create/update/delete, read_query, describe, Dataverse skills, and file upload/download.
Microsoft Learn notes that admins must enable and configure the MCP server and allowed clients for a Power Platform environment before clients such as GitHub Copilot or Claude can connect.

Microsoft Learn says external AI-agent access to Dataverse MCP tools is charged starting December 15, 2025, with Dynamics 365 Premium or Microsoft 365 Copilot USL exceptions for some Dynamics 365 data access.
Microsoft Learn documents a preview MCP endpoint at /api/mcp_preview for enabled environments, while /api/mcp remains the standard GA endpoint.
The GitHub repository showed 160 stars, 43 forks, 49 commits, and a June 24, 2026 latest commit when researched on July 3, 2026.

angles: Write the guide as a production-minded walkthrough: install, connect, run the first prompt, inspect what changed, validate results, and decide whether it is safe to promote.
Lead with the new operating model: enterprise app development shifts from clicking through portals or scripting APIs to supervising an agent that can use Dataverse-native tools.

Make governance the differentiator: environment selection, allowed MCP clients, least-privilege roles, destructive-action approvals, audit logs, and solution packaging should be explicit prerequisites.
Translate the Build 2026 Zava Coffee examples into reusable prompt patterns for data model creation, CRM operations, and security administration.
Explain tool selection under the hood: PAC CLI for auth/solutions, MCP for metadata/data operations, Python SDK for bulk loads, and Web API for schema or advanced operations.
Include a cost and licensing checkpoint because external MCP tool calls can create Copilot Credit implications.
Beat competitor content by adding troubleshooting tables and validation checklists instead of treating one successful prompt as proof the app is production-ready.
Position Dataverse Skills as agent knowledge, while Dataverse MCP is the governed tool surface; readers often conflate the two.
Create a buyer/admin sidebar: who should enable this now, who should wait, and what policies should be in place before broad rollout.
